value: EXTERN ARRAY-BOUND CENSUS, image-wide, measured 2026-09-02 at commit 880cc0e8e in worktree GDL-Claude-ToolQueue7 (branch claude/tool-queue-7-20260903, base cf81a9103). 328 `extern T name[N];` declarations across src/ and include/ carry a sized symbol in config/GUNE5D/symbols.txt; 90 DISAGREE with it. THE PREMISE THAT COMMISSIONED THIS: UB found ONE wrong bound by hand and it was score-decisive -- `extern char lbl_80347F4C[12]` at src/game/ui/select.c:101 where symbols.txt gives size:0x8; 12 sits above MWCC's 8-byte small-data threshold and 8 below it, so the bound changes the ADDRESSING FORM the compiler selects (our lis+addi against the target's single `li rN,0 @lbl_80347F4C(EMB_SDA21)`) -- see attempt.UB_update-class-spec-branch-pair-plus-sdata-size-are-one-coupled-lever.20260902.v1. THE MOST IMPORTANT RESULT IS NOT THE 90. A flat mismatch list would be MISLEADING, because the sizes in symbols.txt are not all declared sizes -- many are inferred by dtk from the layout. gPlayers is recorded `size:0x9F1` (2545 bytes), which is not divisible by 4 and therefore cannot be the size of a 4-element player array at all, while the source's `[4][0x335C]` is plainly the real shape. Reporting 90 rows as 90 source bugs would repeat the sizing error claim.law.MC_the-unabsorbed-census-scores-the-postprocessed-object...20260902.v1 records, in a new place. Rows are therefore bucketed against the DISTANCE TO THE NEXT SYMBOL in the same section. VALIDATION: UB's independently confirmed row lands in over_declared_overlaps, the SMALLEST bucket -- the one built to be actionable -- rather than being swept into the 46-row weak bucket. BUCKET 1, over_declared_overlaps (9): the declaration runs past the next symbol, so either the bound or the map is wrong. It splits by section. Four are large .bss objects where the SOURCE shape is corroborated and the map size is the suspect: controls.c:568 gPlayers[4][0x335C] 52592B vs 2545B; critter.c:360 lbl_802411B0[0x540] 1344B vs 84B; mb_model.c:85 lbl_802A5CF0[0x4C4] 1220B vs 28B; btricol.c:48 lbl_8023F7E8[8] 32B vs 16B. Five are small .sdata2/.sbss objects -- UB's confirmed class, where the bound drives the small-data addressing decision and is therefore SCORE-VISIBLE: select.c:101 lbl_80347F4C[12] 12B vs 8B (CONFIRMED by UB); gamemain.c:4515 lbl_80346C48[8] 8B vs 1B; gamemain.c:3120 lbl_80346AA0[8] 8B vs 3B; memcard.c:209 lbl_80344A10[2] 8B vs 4B; screensaver.c:846 lbl_803473FC[6] 6B vs 4B. BUCKET 2, under_declared (35): the source sees FEWER bytes than the linker records, so the linker size is corroborated by real data and the bound is the suspect. Highest-value rows: critter.c:561 gIdentityMatrix[12] 48B vs 64B -- 64 bytes is the 16 floats of a 4x4 matrix, so [12] is simply wrong; recorder.c:30 AND camera.c:361 both declare gCameraTargetPositions[7][3] 84B vs 108B (27 floats), the same symbol under-declared in two TUs; mb_main.c:33 lbl_802C45CC[16] 64B vs 388B; gauntworld.c:4338 lbl_8011C904[8] 32B vs 204B; world.c:148 lbl_8028C9A8[64] 64B vs 228B; screensaver.c:172 lbl_8011DCBC[3] 12B vs 100B; sfx.c:263 lbl_80122E60[4] 16B vs 68B; pb_objregs.c:412 lbl_802C5538[4] 16B vs 64B; mb_window.c:99 lbl_802A4B30[4] 16B vs 24B; sfx.c:223 gFloorCollisionResult[16] 64B vs 72B; mb_main.c:45 lbl_802A4D48[1001] 4004B vs 4008B (off by one element). BUCKET 3, over_declared_within_gap (46): declared exceeds the recorded size but still fits before the next symbol, which is exactly what an inferred size looks like. Weakest bucket, screen individually, do not sweep. NOT CLEARED, MERELY UNMEASURED: 56 declarations whose element is a struct or typedef this tool cannot size, and 5 whose symbol carries no size in symbols.txt. HANDOFF: this lane is measure-and-report only and edited NO source; the RS lane owns the fixes. Full rows including the 46-row bucket: re-run the tool with --out. THE CHEAP SCREEN FOR A CONSUMER: never fix a row from this census on the mismatch alone -- read the object's own accesses first, because the census cannot tell which SIDE of a disagreement is wrong, only that the two disagree.
